cells.tense: The picture you carry holds up because the hours are already inside it.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Take whatever you keep picturing and do one small piece of it today — not the whole plan, just the first piece you'd choose if nobody were watching.
cells.core:
The picture holds up because the hours are already inside it. Little in it is borrowed. That's why acting on it now costs less than talking yourself into it later — something is already moving that way, and the direction holds.

The step ahead is lit and the rest of the road isn't, and that's enough to work with. The direction came from what you actually care about, not from waiting for the whole thing to appear. Put today's effort into the piece you can already make out. A picture that's real gets built a piece at a time, and the next piece shows up once this one is standing.
cells.sheetLine: The picture is real, so move on the lit step.
cells.verb: Walking into the dark with light for one step
cells.place: standing back far enough to see the whole of it while still inside it

cells.tense: The whole road is being built in your head before the ground has shown you anything.
cells.act: protect the young thing from being judged early
cells.ask: Pick the idea you keep testing against how it will really go — keep it to yourself for a week, show nobody, let it stay rough.
cells.core:
Out here the whole road gets built before the ground has shown anything. Every dark stretch acquires a picture, and the pictures get heavier than the walking. It reads as depth from inside. From outside it looks like a dream already treated as true, and what was meant to grow keeps getting measured against the version in your head.

An idea is a young thing. Keep this one away from your own verdict for a while — no testing it against how it will really go, no showing it around for the reaction. Give it what it needs today and expect nothing back. What's in your head isn't the thing yet, and leaving it small and unproven is how it turns into something real.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in the plan, not the thing.

cells.tense: The way of seeing you set down a while back is still the one you're standing on.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: Take what you're dealing with and put the first read you had of it on paper — a single line, left alone, unexamined.
cells.core:
You stopped trusting how you used to see things. So nothing comes through unless it can be proven first, and the whole pattern stays out of reach. You work from the literal piece at hand instead, which is real but small.

There's a knowing that arrives before the reasons — it was there before the argument against it appeared. It doesn't need defending, only noticing. Take what you're dealing with, put the first read you had of it on paper, before you explained anything, and leave that line unexamined. Don't check it. What gets attended to grows, and you're allowed to attend to what you already see.
cells.sheetLine: Something in you reads the room already. Start there.

cells.tense: You've been shaping how the week goes by a picture you haven't looked at directly.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Sit alone for ten minutes with whatever picture of your life you're carrying — no writing, no deciding, just sit with what's there, then close it.
cells.core:
A picture of how things should go has been steering the week, and you'd say you're just getting on. It's in the work you pick, the people you keep close, the version of a good life you measure against. The picture is running things quietly, and its hand stays invisible from where you sit.

There's a plainer form of this that came before the picture got complicated, and a small alone practice brings it back into view. Ten minutes, no audience, no plan. Sit with what you're actually picturing your life becoming and watch it without steering it. That's the whole practice. The imagining is yours, and this is where your own hand becomes visible.
cells.sheetLine: A picture is steering the week. Look at it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person can already see from outside the system while inside it — the record gives Recognition as the seat capacity, not as something the person reliably does. The reader could object that this has never been true for them; the ask survives that, since it is a several-minute practice that teaches something even if the person never recognises patterns well. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'There is already light on the next step' in the Balanced core, which is a promise I would be making on the record's behalf rather than offering.
